About Upstart

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.
The Team: 

Upstart's Growth team is dedicated to creating a seamless product experience that allows customers to effortlessly discover and access Upstart's credit products, both for the first time and on an ongoing basis. By building exceptional, customer-centric experiences, this team plays a crucial role in making Upstart the premier destination for consumer credit, driving growth and unifying Upstart's product portfolio into a cohesive, multi-product marketplace.

As a Principal Product Manager, you will own the strategy and evolution of Upstart's end-to-end credit conversion experience, helping users move from intent, to the right credit offering, to approval and funding. You'll identify and solve the highest-leverage points of friction across the funnel, creating an experience that feels intelligently matched, transparent, and human while driving meaningful growth for the business.

This is a role with room to take big swings. Upstart has built a strong optimization muscle, and the next chapter is less about tuning individual screens and more about fundamentally rethinking how we engage users on their way to getting funded and achieving their financial goals.

How you’ll make an impact

• Own and evolve the strategy for Upstart's end-to-end conversion experience, from application start through offer acceptance and beyond.

• Take on the hardest conversion problems with a customer-first mindset, such as helping users whose offer differs from what they requested understand their options and move forward with confidence.

• Optimize across Upstart's credit portfolio, growing the core personal loan business while helping users find the product that best fits their needs.

• Set the success metrics for your area and use them to prioritize the highest-ROI opportunities, experimenting where an experiment is the right way to decide.

• Turn data into decisions, segmenting aggressively since aggregate conversion rates often mask very different user problems.

• Build deep customer understanding alongside research, consumer insights, and product marketing so the borrower experience feels intuitive and human.

• Influence without direct authority across engineering, design, analytics, ML, marketing, compliance, and executive leadership, creating clarity where ownership crosses teams.

• Use GenAI as a real extension of your toolkit: synthesizing qualitative inputs, running exploratory analysis, and prototyping concepts to sharpen product conversations.

What we're looking for

• Minimum Qualifications 

• 8+ years of product management experience, including significant B2C ownership of high-scale mobile and desktop consumer experiences with proven business impact

• Demonstrated success materially improving a complex conversion funnel through a combination of product strategy, experimentation, analytics, and customer insight, with a track record of leading a team to specific KPIs (e.g., conversion improvements, revenue)

• Exceptional quantitative judgment, with the ability to assess funnel data, segment behavior, size opportunities, interpret experiments, and recognize unintended downstream effects

• Strong experimentation instincts, including hypothesis development, experiment design, A/B testing, funnel and results analysis, and knowing when a test is (or is not) the right decision-making mechanism

• Strong consumer product intuition, particularly around high-consideration decisions involving trust, uncertainty, or meaningful tradeoffs

• Ability to move fluidly, and quickly, between strategic questions (“What fundamentally prevents users from getting what they came for?”) and detailed product questions (“What exactly should happen on this screen for this user segment?”)

• Track record of leading complex cross-functional initiatives and aligning diverse stakeholders, from executive leaders to cross-functional partners, without relying on organizational authority

• Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to turn ambiguous problems into clear priorities and decisions

• Preferred Qualifications

• Experience in fintech, lending, financial services, marketplaces, insurance, or another regulated, high-consideration industry

• Experience with personalization, recommendation systems, matching, pricing, or ML-powered consumer experiences

• Familiarity with identity, bank linking, income verification, Plaid, or similar financial-data infrastructure

• Proven track record of building and scaling multi-product ecosystems or marketplaces in a B2C environment

Travel requirements As a digital first company, the majority of your work can be accomplished remotely. The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions’ cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time.

In 1933, Harry Beck introduced a radically different map of the London Underground. Rather than faithfully depicting the geography of London, he simplified the sprawling transit network into clean lines, clear connections, and a system that anyone could navigate. Distances were distorted, angles were standardized, and unnecessary details disappeared. The result was something far more useful than a geographically accurate map: a way for millions of people to understand a complex system and confidently find their way through it.

Beck understood something fundamental. The best way to explain something complicated isn't to show people everything. It's to understand what matters to them and make that unmistakably clear.

At Mercury, we believe great product marketing works the same way. Banking* and payments can be complex, but the value they create for customers shouldn't be. Our job is to understand what people need, find the essence of what we're building, and help customers see how it can make their lives better.

We're a financial technology company building products that help ambitious businesses do more with their money. From everyday banking and payments to international money movement and emerging capabilities like agentic payments, we're making complex financial workflows feel remarkably simple.

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager to help bring these products to market, communicate their value, and make sure customers discover and use what we're building.

This role sits at the intersection of Product, Marketing, and Revenue. You'll develop positioning, lead go-to-market strategies, drive successful product launches, and identify opportunities to increase adoption and revenue.

We care deeply about craft, but successful product marketing is about more than a beautiful campaign or a well-executed announcement. It's about understanding customers, building an effective plan, and driving meaningful results.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

In this role, you'll:

• Lead impactful product launches. Own end-to-end go-to-market strategy and execution for new banking and payments capabilities, including emerging agentic features. Develop launch plans, align cross-functional teams, prepare customer-facing partners, and measure impact on product adoption and business goals.

• Get close to our customers. Build a deep understanding of how founders and finance teams manage money, what challenges they face, and why they choose one financial product over another. Turn these insights into compelling positioning, messaging, and GTM strategies.

• Execute AI-first. Use AI to work smarter, move faster, and produce better outcomes. You’ll build and use existing workflows, automations, and repeatable processes that improve how you approach research, launch execution, competitive intelligence, and other core responsibilities.

• Help more customers discover and use Mercury. Partner with Product, Lifecycle, Activation, and Revenue to drive adoption of banking and payments capabilities. Identify growth opportunities, test hypotheses, and improve product usage over time.

• Become an expert on our market. Develop a sharp understanding of the banking and payments competitive landscape, including emerging fintech products and traditional financial institutions. Translate market insights into differentiated positioning and actionable recommendations.

• Equip our Revenue teams to win. Build trusted relationships with customer-facing teams and develop the competitive intelligence, battlecards, messaging, and training they need to communicate Mercury's value confidently and accurately.

• Work with exceptional cross-functional partners. Collaborate with Product, Brand, Creative, Lifecycle, and Revenue to bring go-to-market strategies to life. Help shape strong campaign briefs and channel strategies, drawing on specialized creative expertise when needed.

• Connect marketing to business impact. Define clear objectives for launches and growth initiatives, track meaningful performance indicators, and communicate what worked, what didn't, and what we should do next.

• Own the full picture. Manage multiple projects and product areas simultaneously, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and prioritize the work that will have the greatest impact on Mercury and its customers.

You might be a great fit if you:

• Have 2-3 years of B2B product marketing experience and have taken meaningful ownership of product launches and go-to-market initiatives.

• Have successfully brought new products or features to market and can explain the business impact of your work.

• Know how to build a complete GTM strategy, from customer insight and positioning through launch execution, field readiness, and post-launch measurement.

• Are an AI-native operator who goes beyond using AI for basic tasks. You've built workflows, automations, or systems that meaningfully improve the efficiency or quality of your work and your team's, and you're constantly experimenting with new ways to work better.

• Are deeply curious about customers and naturally look for the insights behind their behaviors, needs, and decisions.

• Can translate complex products and capabilities into clear, compelling messaging.

• Understand that great product marketing extends beyond launches into product adoption, competitive positioning, and revenue growth.

• Are comfortable using customer feedback, data, and experimentation to evaluate and improve marketing performance.

• Enjoy working closely with Product, Marketing, and Revenue teams and know how to build trusted relationships across functions.

• Can manage several competing priorities, make good decisions with incomplete information, and independently move important work forward.

• Experience in fintech, banking*, or payments is a plus, but it's not required. We're equally interested in people who have done exceptional work in other B2B industries and are excited to learn something new.

Who We Are
Hi, we're DuckDuckGo, the online protection company and remote-first team of 400+ on a mission to raise the standard of trust online. Founded in 2008 and profitable since 2014, our annual revenue is in the hundreds of millions USD and millions use our browser on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, our search engine, and the DuckDuckGo subscription. We also offer private, useful, and optional AI, including Duck.ai, which lets you chat privately with ChatGPT, Claude, and other AIs, all in one place. 
 
Our culture of trust, inclusivity, and empowered project management underpins everything we do, where each team member takes full ownership of their projects, from scoping and execution to postmortem. If you're seeking end-to-end ownership of your work, you've come to the right place!

Your Team and Role
Working on the Web Dependability Engineering team, you'll make sure websites just work in DuckDuckGo's browsers across Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, helping ensure our users have the best-possible experience browsing with DuckDuckGo. Recent projects include:
• 
Reverse-engineering how sites detect our privacy protections and building countermeasures that keep pages working
• 
Shimming browser APIs so sites work seamlessly across different browser engines and system webviews
• 
Building LLM agent pipelines that automatically reproduce and triage reported site breakage
 
As a Senior Web Compatibility Engineer, you'll be our resident expert on why websites break and how to fix them: owning the webcompat side of our triage process, debugging gnarly issues in code you don't control, distinguishing site bugs from browser bugs from privacy protection-induced breakage, leading the charge when a top site breaks and becomes an incident, shipping durable fixes across every platform, and work on related projects that prevent user churn and keep users coming back to DuckDuckGo.

7+ years of experience building and debugging complex web applications with vanilla JavaScript.

Business Solutions Partner — GTM & Finance Systems

Location
Costa Rica

Position Summary

6sense is seeking an Enterprise AI Business Solutions Partner to help transform how business functions leverage AI, automation, and enterprise technology to achieve their goals.

This role sits at the intersection of business consulting, AI solution design, automation engineering, and value realization. You will partner with teams across Go-to-Market, Customer Success, Support, Legal, Finance, and Partner Operations to identify opportunities where AI and automation can simplify work, improve user experiences, reduce costs, and accelerate business outcomes.

Unlike a traditional Business Systems Analyst or Business Solution Partner, this role is expected to move beyond requirements gathering. You will evaluate business processes, build proof-of-concepts, create AI agents, develop low-code automations, and validate business value before solutions are scaled into production. Working closely with the Enterprise AI Engineering team, you will translate complex business challenges into technical requirements and implementation plans while independently delivering design prototypes and lightweight solutions using platforms such as Microsoft Copilot, Claude, Workato, and other approved enterprise AI technologies.

A successful candidate combines strong business analysis skills with hands-on technical aptitude. They can engage stakeholders, map workflows, build basic automations, create AI-powered solutions, measure outcomes, and communicate recommendations to both business and technical audiences.

This is a growth role within a new Enterprise AI career track. You will work under the guidance of the Lead Enterprise AI Business Solutions Engineer and will be measured on business outcomes, including adoption, productivity gains, automation impact, cost avoidance, and process improvements. As you progress, you will take increasing ownership of a portfolio of business capabilities, including identifying, developing, delivering and maturing measurable AI-driven value.

Responsibilities

Tool Inventory & AI Efficiency Discovery

• Build and maintain the AI and tool inventory for your assigned function: owner, use case, active users, annual cost, renewal date, AI features in use, contract exit terms and replacement feasibility.

• Find where AI features we already pay for are unused, duplicated or overlap with other tools, and document the findings.

• Track renewal dates and flag every contract at least 120 days before the notice date so a build-vs-buy decision can be made in time.

• Run discovery interviews and working sessions with stakeholders to understand how work actually gets done, and surface the business problem behind the requested feature.

• Map current processes and estimate the time spent, the number of people involved and the frequency, so every opportunity has a baseline.

Build-vs-Buy Analysis & Business Cases

• Prepare the inputs for build-vs-buy analysis: what the tool does, how deeply it is integrated, compliance burden, usage compared with cost, and realistic replacement scope.

• Contribute to business cases that compare three-year build, run and support cost with vendor cost, working with the Lead and with Enterprise AI Engineers on the build side.

• Agree baselines with business owners before work starts and record their sign-off, so savings and hours returned can be validated later.

• Recommend which candidates to pursue first, using renewal timing, savings potential and build feasibility.

Prototyping & Applied AI
